name: Acute Motor Axonal Neuropathy
aliases: Acute Motor Axonal Neuropathy variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence reported in East Asia and Central America

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Brighton Criteria for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (adapted for AMAN)

criteria.description: Rapid onset of symmetric weakness predominantly affecting distal limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal motor neuropathy without demyelination
Cerebrospinal fluid showing albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein with normal cell count)
Minimal or no sensory nerve involvement clinically or electrophysiologically
History of preceding infection such as Campylobacter jejuni

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acute symmetric motor weakness with electrophysiological confirmation of axonal motor neuropathy and absence of sensory involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on electrophysiological studies differentiating AMAN from demyelinating variants

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute symmetric flaccid paralysis of distal limbs
searchTerms: sudden weakness in both arms and legs
floppy paralysis affecting hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

common.symptomName: Rapid progression of muscle weakness over days

searchTerms: muscle wasting in arms or legs
problems with eye or face movement

common.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations)
searchTerms: heart rate and blood pressure swings

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness requiring ventilatory support
Mild sensory symptoms such as paresthesias

searchTerms: problems with bladder or bowel function

rare.symptomName: Severe autonomic instability leading to arrhythmias

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal white cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation)
Serologic evidence of recent Campylobacter jejuni infection
imaging: MRI of spine typically normal or may show nerve root enhancement
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; primarily acquired autoimmune etiology
other: Electrophysiological studies showing reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes with normal sensory nerve action potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
Presence of conduction block on electrophysiology

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness with respiratory compromise
Bulbar muscle involvement causing dysphagia or dysarthria
Severe autonomic instability (e.g., cardiac arrhythmias, blood pressure fluctuations)
references: Willison HJ, Jacobs BC, van Doorn PA. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2016 Aug 13;388(10045):717-27.
Orphanet: Acute motor axonal neuropathy - ORPHA:98918
